note: Ground-truth answer key for Flowprint v0.1-alpha benchmark. Medusa's HTTP API is Express served via Medusa's own file-based routing convention (packages/core/framework/src/http/routes-loader.ts), NOT Next.js App Router. The v0.1-alpha analyzer's route scope is Next.js App Router only, so routes[] is intentionally EMPTY and the Medusa route surface is encoded as explicit out-of-scope boundary entries. Only facts re-verified against the cloned tree at the pinned SHA are included; the tree at SHA is ground truth.

ambiguities.detail: 330 route.ts files under packages/medusa/src/api are mapped to method+path by Medusa's routes-loader convention (ROUTE_NAME='route', [param]→:param, named exports ∩ HTTP_METHODS in types.ts:21-29) and served by Express (assembled by ApiLoader in packages/core/framework/src/http/router.ts) — NOT Next.js App Router. Out of v0.1-alpha route scope: the analyzer must NOT emit these as routes. Surfaced as unknown/not-claimed.

Server started via the @medusajs/cli bin (medusa → packages/cli/medusa-cli/cli.js) running loaders in packages/medusa/src/loaders/ (api.ts, index.ts verified at SHA). The exact app.listen call site (inside the CLI package) was not inspected → U. Package.json main/bin entry detection degrades here: the real entry is CLI+loaders, not @medusajs/medusa main.

Feature-flag-disabled route files (isFileSkipped/isFileDisabled referenced in routes-loader.ts) make the effective set Inferred; duplicate-route override order (Promise.all scanDir) makes the winner Unknown. Both beyond v0.1-alpha scope — recorded only so a future Medusa detector knows the boundary.
